title: Criteria to Determine Childcare and Preschool Subsidies
what_it_is: Criteria to Determine Childcare and Preschool Subsidies

sections.label: Basic Subsidy for childcare
sections.summary: The Government provides a universal Basic Subsidy of $150 monthly, or $300 monthly for working mothers, to defray childcare costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To defray the cost of childcare for families, the Government provides a universal Basic Subsidy of $150 per month, or $300 per month for working mothers.

sections.label: Additional Subsidy for working mothers
sections.summary: An Additional Subsidy supports working mothers with monthly household income of $7,500 and below, or per capita income of $1,875 and below.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: An Additional Subsidy was introduced to support working mothers whose monthly household income is $7,500 and below, or whose per capita income is $1,875 and below.

sections.label: KiFAS and child-raising support
sections.summary: In 2015 KiFAS was enhanced for families with monthly household income of $6,000 and below, or per capita income of $1,500 and below, plus Baby Bonus and CDA support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 2015, we also enhanced the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS) to benefit more families whose children are enrolled in kindergartens run by the Anchor Operators (AOPs) or by the Ministry of Education (MOE).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Families with monthly household income of $6,000 and below, or per capita income of $1,500 and below, can benefit from KiFAS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Apart from these subsidies, the Government provides support to defray the costs of child-raising.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These include the Baby Bonus Cash Gift of $8,000 to $10,000 per child, and the Child Development Account (CDA) to which the Government contributes up to $6,000 to $18,000 per child, depending on the child’s birth order and co-savings by parents.

sections.label: AOP fee caps and market share
sections.summary: AOP fees are capped at $720 for full-day childcare and $160 for kindergartens, and such preschools now make up almost half the market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, the fees at AOPs are capped at $720 for full-day childcare and $160 for kindergartens, before Goods and Services Tax.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: A family with a monthly household income of $2,500 or less with a child enrolled in an AOP centre can pay as little as $3 for full-day childcare and $1 for kindergarten services per month, after subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These Government-run and supported preschools now make up almost half of the market, from just one-third of the market five years ago, and have helped to stabilise preschool fees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: These operators are projected to make up two-thirds of the market by 2023.
